issues.legal_issue: A purchaser who acquires land after publication of an acquisition notification has no right to challenge the acquisition proceedings.
material_facts: The petitioner purchased the property after publication of the acquisition notification.
The petitioner challenged the notification, declaration, and award.
issues.conclusion: The petitioner had no right to challenge the acquisition proceedings or the award because its purchase after publication of the notification gave it no valid title.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4(1), 6, and 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, an alienation after publication of the acquisition notification does not bind the State or the beneficiary, and the purchaser acquires no valid title; once possession is taken after the award, the land vests in the State free of encumbrances. The Court relied on Gurmukh Singh v. State of Haryana, Y.N. Garg v. State of Rajasthan, Sneh Prabha v. State of U.P., and U.P. Jal Nigam v. Kalra Properties (P) Ltd.

predicates.acquisition_challenge_proceeding: A person seeks to challenge the legality of land acquisition proceedings.
predicates.purchase_after_acquisition_notification: The person acquired the land after the acquisition notification had been published.
predicates.post_notification_purchaser_lacks_right_: A person who acquired the land after publication of the acquisition notification has no right to challenge the acquisition proceedings.

issues.definition: When a person seeks to challenge land acquisition after acquiring the land following publication of the acquisition notification, that person lacks the right to challenge the acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: Unreasonable delay in seeking extraordinary writ relief to challenge land acquisition may bar the challenge.
material_facts: The acquisition notification was published in 1976, the declaration was published in 1977, and the award was made in 1981.
The petitioner filed its writ petition in 1994, asserting that it had no knowledge of the acquisition proceedings until shortly before filing.
The High Court dismissed the writ petition for laches.
issues.conclusion: The petitioner’s delayed challenge was barred by laches, and the Court found no reason to interfere with the High Court’s dismissal.
issues.legal_principle: The discretionary extraordinary remedies of mandamus, certiorari, or other relief may be denied where a petitioner approaches the court after unreasonable delay; there is no universal rule fixing the effect of delay. The Court relied on State of Madhya Pradesh v. Bhailal Bhai, Rabindranath Bose v. Union of India, and Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. Industrial Development & Investment Co. Pvt. Ltd., among other decisions.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_land_acquisition: A person seeks extraordinary writ relief to challenge land acquisition proceedings.
predicates.unreasonable_delay_in_approaching_court: The person waits an unreasonable period after the acquisition proceedings before approaching the court.
predicates.extraordinary_writ_relief_may_be_denied_: A court may deny extraordinary writ relief because the challenge was brought after unreasonable delay.

issues.definition: When a person seeks extraordinary writ relief against land acquisition after an unreasonable delay, the relief may be denied for laches.
